messages.author: e204e9a8d0f3a7f8
messages.subject: Formula as constraint in model
parts:
Hello,

Does anyone know how to have an external value evaluated as a constraint in the model in Lavaan.

For example, suppose I have

V <- (1-.665)*.55

which equals 0.18425

Then suppose I want to call that value as a parameter constraint in a CFA model such as:

CFA.Model <- '
                  F1 =~ 1*x1
                  x1 ~~ V*x1
                     '
So that the value of V is constraining the residual variance of x1.  It appears that V will not be evaluated as 0.18425 and the model won't run.

I've tried the model constraint function but that won't work as I want the value of V to change.

Thanks,

Scott

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Formula as constraint in model
parts:
> So that the value of V is constraining the residual variance of x1. It
> appears that V will not be evaluated as 0.18425 and the model won't run.

Indeed. That is by design (a long story).

The way to handle this, is write a small function that 'generates'
syntax, where the value of 'V' is filled in.

Something along the lines of:

genMySyntax <- function(V = 1.0) {
txt1 <- "F1 =~ 1*x1"
txt2 <- paste0("x1 ~~ ", V, "*x1")
c(txt1, txt2)
}

# small test
library(lavaan)

Data <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(100))

# reliability of x1 is assumted to be 0.80
x1.rho <- 0.80

# residual variance of x1
V <- (1-x1.rho)*var(Data$x1)

# generate syntax
myModel <- genMySyntax(V = V)

# fit model
fit <- sem(myModel, data = Data)
summary(fit)


Yves.
